title: Assistant Professor in Agricultural and Applied Economics
description:
Salary:

Job Summary:

Job Summary:

The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) in the
College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS), together with the
Division of Extension (EXT) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison,
invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in
community economic development. This is a jointly appointed faculty
position to both AAE and the Department of Extension, with the
tenure home in AAE. Within Extension, the candidate will affiliate
with the Community Development Institute. The position is funded
75% EXT/ 25% CALS and structured as a 12-month appointment. Given
the outreach expectations of the Extension appointment, there is no
requirement for traditional group instruction in the undergraduate
or graduate program.

The ideal candidate has demonstrated research potential in rural
and/or community economic development and complements existing
departmental strengths in agricultural, environmental, community,
and/or development economics. We seek candidates with evidence of
the ability to combine rigorous economic research with effective
outreach and who have demonstrated a strong commitment to public
engagement and real-world impact.

As a faculty member, the candidate will lead regionally and
nationally recognized research, outreach, and educational
programming focused on community economic development within the
United States, with relevance to Wisconsin. They will design and
conduct applied research to address challenges facing rural
communities. The faculty member will translate research findings
into practical, accessible resources for stakeholders, such as
local governments, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders.
The faculty member is expected to support the university’s mission
of fostering inclusive, sustainable community growth, as well as
the scholarly life of the department through collegial engagement,
mentorship, and service.

This position offers an outstanding opportunity for impact by
working at a top land-grant institution, joining an established
network of community development professionals across the state and
nationally, and working directly with local leaders and
communities.

Additional Information:

At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the Division of Extension
collaborates with many departments to hire, fund, and tenure
faculty who generate research directly applicable to Wisconsin
communities and outreach in support of Extension programming. These
co-funded faculty work collaboratively with Extension educators,
other faculty, and external partners through research, outreach,
and extramural funding opportunities related to their
subject-matter expertise. While tenured in the department of their
field of study, Extension activities are a significant portion of
their duties and performance evaluation.



The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at UW–Madison
is internationally recognized for its research and teaching in
agricultural, environmental, community, and development economics.
Faculty collaborate across disciplines to address complex global
and local challenges. UW–Madison is located in Madison,
Wisconsin—an innovative and vibrant city frequently ranked among
the best places to live in the U.S. The university fosters a
collaborative and inclusive environment and is committed to
diversity, equity, and community engagement.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Publish scholarly and applied research on community economic
development in U.S. and relevant to communities in Wisconsin on
topics such as workforce development, housing, entrepreneurship,
local government capacity, and regional economic resilience.
Develop an extension program that translates and applies
research-based knowledge and methods to issues and problems facing
Wisconsin communities and document the impact of these
efforts.
Work with interdisciplinary teams within CALS, Extension, and
across UW–Madison, to advance integrated approaches to solving
real-world challenges in Wisconsin and rural America.
Engage with stakeholders, including industry leaders,
policymakers, and community groups on community development
issues.
Secure extramural funding to support research and
programming.
Mentor students at all levels and contribute to curriculum
development.
Participate in departmental, college, and university
committees, as well as relevant professional associations and
public service activities.
Contribute to a supportive and inclusive academic
environment.

Department: Agricultural and Applied Economics
Compensation: Negotiable, 12-month

Required Qualifications:

Training or experience demonstrating potential for excellence
in conducting frontier research and actively engaging in
outreach.
Demonstrated skill in statistical data analysis, managing large
datasets, and complex problem-solving.
Demonstrated subject-matter expertise in relevant topic areas
such as community economic development, rural development, and
regional science.
A record of, or demonstrated potential for, securing
competitive external funding.
Demonstrated ability or potential for strong public engagement,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and stakeholder engagement.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required and
will be assessed via written work listed on curriculum vitae,
statements submitted for the application, and interactions during
the interview process.


Education:

Required: Ph.D. in Agricultural Economics, Economics, or a related
field, such as Urban and Regional Planning or Public Policy, by the
start date.

How to Apply:

Apply online at "Jobs at UW" (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under job
number JR10015766. Applications must be received through
UW-Madison's online application system.

To begin the process, please click "".

Applicants must upload the following information as a single PDF
document:

1) Cover letter detailing interest and relevant training/experience
for this position (1-page)

2) Curriculum vitae

3) Statements of:

a. Extension or Outreach philosophy and experience (2-page
limit)

b. Research experience and interests with a description of current
and planned research (2 page limit).

4) An example of research such as a job market paper.

5) Contact information for two to three references who will submit
letters of recommendation and may be contacted for a reference
phone call at a later date.

The deadline for assuring full consideration is November 8, 2026;
however, the position will remain open, and applications may be
considered until the position is filled.
